questions.q: I find new ideas more interesting than familiar ones.
I enjoy thinking about abstract concepts.
I keep appointments and rarely run late.
I finish what I start, even when it gets dull.
I feel energised by spending time with strangers.
I prefer a loud party to a quiet evening.
I try to keep the peace, even at some cost.
I trust people until they give me reason not to.
I worry about things I can't control.
Small setbacks throw off my whole day.
I stick with what I know works rather than experiment.
I leave things to the last minute more often than not.
A full day alone recharges me more than a night out.
I'd rather win the argument than smooth things over.
It takes a lot to rattle me.
I go looking for music, films or books I know nothing about.
I have little patience for questions with no practical use.
I keep my things in order without having to think about it.
My plans tend to fall apart in the details.
I start conversations with people I have just met.
In a group I say less than most people there.
I give people the benefit of the doubt when a story doesn't add up.
I decide quickly whether someone is worth my time.
I replay conversations afterwards, looking for what I got wrong.
I sleep fine the night before something big.

deep.q: I get tense about things that haven't happened yet.
A small noise at night is enough to put me on edge.
I rarely feel nervous, even when there is reason to.
I can wait for bad news without it eating at me.
When I'm treated unfairly, it burns for a long time.
A stranger being rude can spoil my whole mood.
People who know me would say I almost never get angry.
I let insults go without much effort.
Some days I can't find the energy to start anything.
I go through stretches where nothing seems worth the effort.
I'm mostly at peace with who I am.
Getting out of bed is rarely a struggle for me.
I often wonder what people thought of me after I've left.
Being laughed at is one of the worst things I can imagine.
I can look foolish in public and shrug it off.
Whether strangers approve of me rarely crosses my mind.
Once I start on something I enjoy, stopping is the hard part.
I often buy or eat things I told myself I wouldn't.
A craving passes if I just wait it out.
Saying no to a second helping comes easily to me.
When too much comes at once, I freeze.
In a crisis I need someone else to tell me what to do.
I think clearly when everything is going wrong.
Pressure sharpens me rather than scatters me.
I make friends quickly wherever I go.
I let new people see straight away that I like them.
It takes me a long time to warm to someone.
I keep most people at arm's length.
The busier a place is, the more I enjoy it.
I'd join a big group of people I barely know rather than stay home.
Crowds drain me faster than anything else.
I avoid places where I'll be one face in a crowd.
When a group can't decide, I usually end up deciding for it.
I say what I want plainly, even to people senior to me.
I'd rather follow a good plan than have to make one.
I let other people steer, even when I disagree.
I like my days packed from morning to night.
I walk fast, eat fast and talk fast.
I'd rather do one thing slowly than three things quickly.
An empty afternoon with nothing planned is a gift.
I chase the kind of thrill that makes my heart race.
Loud, bright, fast places make me feel alive.
I avoid anything that promises an adrenaline rush.
The safest option is usually the one I want.
I laugh easily and often.
Most mornings I wake up in a good mood.
People have called me hard to excite.
I don't get carried away by good news.
I spend a lot of time in daydreams.
I invent whole stories about strangers I see on the bus.
I'd rather deal with facts than fantasies.
Make-believe stopped interesting me when I grew up.
A piece of music can stop me in my tracks.
I'll go out of my way to see something beautiful.
Art galleries bore me.
I don't notice whether a room is beautiful or plain.
I can usually name exactly what I'm feeling.
My moods are a big part of how I experience a day.
I'm often the last to notice that something has upset me.
Talking about feelings feels like a foreign language.
I'll take a new route home just to see something different.
Given the choice, I'd try the dish I can't pronounce.
I order the same thing every time at a restaurant I like.
Change for its own sake makes me uneasy.
A good argument about ideas is my idea of fun.
I'll read something difficult just to see if I can follow it.
I'd rather fix a real problem than debate a philosophical one.
Brain-teasers feel like a waste of an evening.
Rules deserve to be questioned, not just followed.
I'm drawn to people who break with how things are usually done.
Traditions hold a society together and shouldn't be tampered with.
If something has worked for generations, that is reason enough to keep it.
I assume people mean what they say.
Most people would return a wallet they found.
When a deal looks generous, I look for the catch.
I've been let down often enough to expect it.
I say what I think even when a small lie would be smoother.
I'd rather lose an advantage than mislead someone to keep it.
A little flattery is a fair way to get what you want.
I tell people what they want to hear when it serves me.
Helping someone out is one of the best parts of my week.
I'll stop what I'm doing to give directions to a lost stranger.
Requests for help usually feel like an imposition.
Other people's problems are theirs to solve.
I can't stand confrontations.
I hate to seem pushy.
I have a sharp tongue and I use it.
I contradict people more than I agree with them.
I'm uncomfortable when people praise me.
I'd rather let my work speak than talk about it.
I know I'm better at most things than the people around me.
When something goes well, I make sure people know it was me.
Someone else's bad news can ruin my day.
I give money to people on the street even when I doubt their story.
I judge a situation by the facts, not by who is suffering.
Sob stories don't move me much.
When I take something on, I know I'll manage it.
I handle whatever comes up without much fuss.
I often doubt that I'm up to what is asked of me.
Things go wrong for me more than for most people.
I make lists, and I actually use them.
I like a plan for the day before the day starts.
My desk looks like a storm passed through it.
I find things by remembering where I last dropped them.
A promise is a promise, even when keeping it costs me.
I follow rules I disagree with until they are changed.
Rules are for people who can't judge for themselves.
If nobody would know, I'd skip the obligation.
Good enough is never quite good enough for me.
I set goals most people would call ambitious.
I do what's needed and not much more.
I'm happy to coast when nobody is watching.
I can make myself work when I'd rather not.
Distractions rarely pull me off a task.
I need a deadline breathing down my neck to get going.
Half-finished projects pile up around me.
I sleep on big decisions before I make them.
I think through what could go wrong before I say yes.
I say the first thing that comes into my head.
I've made big purchases on the spot and regretted it later.

questions.q: Markets, left to themselves, distribute fairly.
Essential services belong in public hands, not markets.
Some speech is harmful enough to restrict.
The state should keep out of private life.
My country should help others before its own poor.
Borders should be more open than they are now.
Climate action is worth real economic cost.
Green rules should hold even when jobs are on the line.
New technology, on balance, makes life better.
Some technologies should be slowed down on purpose.
Strong leaders matter more than strong institutions.
The system is rigged against ordinary people.
Lower taxes matter more than more public services.
More surveillance is a fair price for more safety.
My country should put its own people first.
The dangers of climate change are exaggerated.
Progress means building first and fixing problems as they come.
Experts and institutions usually get it right.
People mostly end up where their own effort puts them.
The gap between rich and poor is the biggest problem we have.
Order in the streets matters more than the right to protest.
Adults should be free to harm themselves if they choose.
Immigration has made my country better.
We should fix problems at home before problems abroad.
I would pay noticeably more for energy to cut emissions faster.
Environmental rules are already strict enough.
I would rather live with the risks of new technology than miss what it brings.
New tools should prove they are safe before anyone can use them.
Most politicians are in it for themselves.
The people running things mostly know what they are doing.

deep.q: Higher earners should pay a much larger share in tax.
People should keep more of what they earn, even if inequality grows.
Businesses need firm rules to behave well.
Most regulation does more harm than good.
Health, schools and transport work best run by the state.
Private providers usually deliver services better than governments.
People should be free to say things others find offensive.
Some speech does enough harm that it should be banned.
Cameras and data-gathering are a fair price for safety.
The police already have more power than they need.
What adults do in private is none of the state's business.
Society is right to set limits on how people live.
Immigration should be lower than it is now.
People should be freer to move between countries.
We should look after our own before helping other countries.
Rich countries owe real help to poorer ones.
Protecting local industry is worth paying more for goods.
Free trade makes everyone better off in the end.
Climate change is an emergency that justifies drastic action.
We are moving faster on climate than we can afford.
Wild places should be protected even when they could be put to use.
Land is there to be used, not fenced off.
A cleaner environment is worth slower growth.
When jobs and green rules clash, jobs should win.
AI should be allowed to develop with few limits.
Automation is taking more from people than it gives.
Editing genes to prevent disease should go ahead.
We should be very careful about altering human biology.
I'd trade some privacy for services that work better.
Companies collect far too much data about us.
Courts, parliaments and the press mostly do their jobs.
Our institutions serve themselves, not the public.
On hard questions, experts should carry more weight than public opinion.
Experts are often wrong and rarely held to account.
Big decisions should go to a public vote, not politicians.
Representatives make better decisions than referendums.

questions.q: Future generations will live better than ours.
Most of what's changing right now is change for the better.
What I owe my family weighs more than what I owe strangers.
I'd give up real comfort to help a stranger.
Pleasure needs no justification.
Obligations come before enjoyment.
Suffering can give life meaning, not just pain.
A hard life spent on something big beats an easy one.
There are objective right answers in ethics.
Some things are wrong in every era and every culture.
Beauty matters as much as truth.
A beautiful thing needs no other use.
The world is mostly getting worse.
A stranger's suffering moves me as much as a neighbour's.
Enjoying myself is a good enough reason to do something.
A calm, happy life beats a hard, important one.
Right and wrong depend on the culture you're standing in.
Whether something works matters more than how it looks.
I expect my own life ten years from now to be better than it is today.
The problems ahead of us are bigger than anything we have solved.
A life saved far away counts the same as one saved here.
Charity should start with the people around you.
I plan my week around things I will enjoy.
I feel uneasy resting while work is unfinished.
The best parts of my life came out of something difficult.
I would trade a smaller life for a more peaceful one.
Some acts would be wrong even if everyone approved of them.
Morality is something people invented, like money.
I will pay more for something well made when a plain one would do.
Decoration is the first thing I would cut.

attachment.title: Social
attachment.tag: 25 questions · what kind of friend you are

questions.q: I show people I care without being asked.
I'm quick with a hug or a kind word.
Friends know I'll show up when it matters.
Once you're my friend, you're my friend for years.
I say what I'm feeling rather than keeping it in.
I let people see the messy parts of me.
I'm usually the one keeping things light and fun.
I'd rather joke around than be too serious.
Little gets under my skin in a friendship.
I give people room and don't keep score.
Showing affection doesn't come naturally to me.
My friendships tend to fade when life gets busy.
I keep my problems to myself.
I take most things seriously, even the small stuff.
I keep track of who reached out last.
I tell my friends what they mean to me.
Compliments feel awkward coming out of my mouth.
I still keep up with people I met years ago.
When someone moves away, we usually lose touch.
I will admit it when I am struggling.
There are things about me nobody in my life knows.
I am the one who suggests something daft.
I find it hard to switch off and mess about.
A friend cancelling on me barely registers.
It bothers me when a friend doesn't reply for days.
